simplify the process of sending
requests to those OpenAI servers and
extracting the responses you get back.

have to talk about pricing, though.

you're used to either using them for
free or paying a flat subscription fee

APIs. There, you pay for
usage. And all those API

pricing pages, you'll find information

tokens, so for input and
output in the end. And remember,
tokens are, in the end, these things your words
are converted to, as you learned in the deep
dive behind-the-scenes section earlier in the course.
Now the prices here, at the moment where I'm recording
this, for the OpenAI API, are
per million tokens. So if
you were to send a million tokens
to the AI API into the
AI model, so if the AI model has to process
one million tokens, and I were to use
this GPT-4.5 model, and as you
see, there are many models to choose from, but if I were to
use this one, at the moment we're recording this,
then I would pay $75 for those
one million tokens. And of course, this
will not be charged in one-million-token
increments, but instead, every single token will be
charged, and you'll pay a fraction of that if you have a
fraction of the tokens. So every use of
the API will be charged, just to make that very clear.
And for the output that's generated by the model and that's
sent back to your application, you'll also be
charged. And if you hit the
API multiple times, if you interact with it multiple
times, and you send one million tokens to it
multiple times, you'll pay multiple times.
And of course, again, not just per one million tokens.
That's just how the price is determined here, but
for every single token, you're going to pay.

of. That's also why in
order to use these APIs, you have to
